title: Inference config simulations: synthetic workload sweep notes (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This note captures an experimental plan and early findings from a set of spreadsheet-driven cost simulations we used to explore inference-config tradeoffs across batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization knobs. Goal is to produce 3 deployment-ready presets (latency-first, cost-first, balanced) and a short checklist for measurement and rollout.

Context / motivation (short):
- Customers ask for concrete presets they can apply to reduce unit costs without degrading quality or violating p95/p99 SLOs.
- Prior docs give high-level heuristics. This is a measurement-first approach: run param sweeps on synthetic workload traces, capture latency percentiles and token cost, then translate to spreadsheet-level recommendations.

Approach overview (what I ran):
1) Synthetic workload generator (repo linked above) produced traces with: short-chat (median 16 tokens), assistant-long-form (median 220 tokens), and mixed-burst (poisson arrival, variable TTL). We included header metadata to simulate repeated prefixes for caching experiments.
2) Runtime config matrix: model variants (base FP16, int8-quantized, nf4-ish profile), batch sizes {1,2,4,8,16}, kv-cache on/off, cache hit rates simulated {0%, 25%, 50%, 75%}, token-length distributions, and CPU pre/post-processing overhead multipliers.
3) For each combination we collected: p50, p95, p99 latencies, throughput (tokens/s), GPU utilization, and per-token cost estimate (GPU time * spot/hr equivalents + negligible infra overhead). Spreadsheets contain formulas used for converting ms->token-cost.

Key spreadsheet notes (columns and formulas to copy):
- columns: config_id | model | q_profile | batch | kv_on | kv_hit_pct | median_seq | p95_ms | p99_ms | tokens_per_sec | gpu_ms_per_token | est_cost_per_1M_tokens_usd | quality_delta_ppx | notes
- est_cost_per_1M_tokens_usd: = (gpu_ms_per_token * 1e-3 * gpu_hour_rate_usd) * 1e6 / 3600  -- includes simple multiplier for overhead (1.08).
- gpu_ms_per_token derived as measured_total_gpu_ms / measured_total_tokens (experiment-level).
- quality_delta_ppx: use a small evaluation harness that runs 200 prompts from our regression set and computes avg perplexity (or embed-sim delta) vs baseline FP16.

High-level findings (summary):
- Batching: small batch sizes (2-4) give the best cost/latency tradeoff for short-chat traces when target p95 <= 150ms. For longer sequences (>128 tokens) medium batches (8) reduce per-token cost substantially with modest p95 increase. Peak GPU utilization and tail latency must be balanced: when many long requests align, large batch sizes cause p99 spikes.
- KV/prefix caching: effective even at 25% hit rates; a 25% hit reduces GPU_ms_per_token by ~18% on average for mixed workloads. Hit-rate sensitivity: improvements are roughly linear until ~60% hit; beyond that marginal returns decline.
- Quantization: int8/NF4 configurations yield 20-35% lower GPU_ms_per_token on the same batch, but quality regressions are workload-dependent. On long-form completion tasks we saw small perplexity regressions (~1.5–3% relative) for nf4-like profiles; for chat-turn generation regressions were negligible in human-viewed samples but measurable in embed-sim.

Tradeoff heuristics we distilled (for spreadsheet presets):
- Latency-first preset: batch 1-2, kv_on true (require client-side prefix caching), prefer fp16 or conservative nf4 with a mandatory regression test suite, target p95 < 150ms for short-chat.
- Cost-first preset: batch 8 (or auto-batch target 8), kv_on true with expected >=30% hit, nf4/int8 if quality delta_ppx < 2% on regression set, accept p95 up to 400ms for longer sequences.
- Balanced preset: batch 4, kv_on true, nf4 for short-chat only, fp16 for long generations; dynamic routing (short->nf4, long->fp16) recommended.

Operational checklist for running these sim sweeps (copy into runbook):
- [ ] Prepare synthetic trace set: include user prefixes from real anonymized traces (privacy safe) and add injected long-tail outliers.
- [ ] Baseline: run FP16 batch sizes 1/4/8 with kv_off and kv_on (record raw logs).
- [ ] Run quantized variants with same batch sweep and keep identical seeds for prompt set.
- [ ] Compute cost spreadsheet metrics and populate columns; flag any config with p99 > target or quality_delta_ppx > 3%.
- [ ] Shortlist 6 candidates (top by est_cost_per_1M with SLO constraints) and run longer soak tests (12h) to capture drift.
- [ ] If quantized candidate passes soak, prepare rollout: canary 1% traffic -> monitor embed-sim / auto-eval / user reported regressions -> 10% -> 100%.

Quality evaluation notes:
- Use combined metrics: embed cosine delta (for semantic parity), perplexity change, and a small human-blind pairwise eval on 120 prompts when feasible.
- Automated gating: reject any quantized config that increases average embed-sim distance > 0.03 (on our set) or increases perplexity > 3%. These thresholds are conservative and adjustable per customer.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (open for discussion):
- How to standardize cost model to include overhead for routing/failover latency (we currently add 8% static). Should be profiled per-region.
- Need a better way to simulate cold-start KV misses in Dedicated pools — current synthetic trace doesn't capture eviction churn.
- Decision boundary for automatic dynamic-routing (short->nf4, long->fp16): need to build a cheap heuristic based on sequence length + recent tail latency signals.

Spreadsheet attachments and where to look:
- local file stub: ./sims/2026-02-synthetic-sweep-v1.xlsx (exported tabs: raw-measurements, cost-model, candidate-ranking).
- key tabs explained: raw-measurements (per-run logs), normalized (per-token ms), cost-model (formulas above), safety-checks (flags for p99/quality), rollout-plan.

Short recommended next steps for product + SRE + Applied ML (this sprint):
1) Product: pick target presets and finalize the rollout gating thresholds (p95/p99/quality).
2) SRE: instrument extra telemetry for KV-hit sources and eviction rates in Dedicated clusters; add an evictions metric exported to the sim framework.
3) Applied ML: run additional quality evals for nf4 profiles on the LLM-regression suite and provide a per-model quality-latency chart.
4) Eng (runtime): prototype quick-routing rule (seq_len threshold) in staging and test interplay with batching/autobatching.

Notes to self / collaboration cues (informal):
- Ethan: can you re-run the mixed-burst trace with the new preproc multiplier (x1.2)? I suspect CPU overhead will shift the sweet spot to smaller batches.
- Mariana: please paste candidate charts into the confluence page and highlight any configs that fail the embed-sim gate.
- Zhihao: want a short script that converts the raw JSON run logs into the spreadsheet columns automatically — the current hand-copy is tedious.

Appendix (short experiments log):
- 2026-02-16: baseline runs completed for fp16 batch 1/4/8; observed p95 120/220/370 ms on short-chat.
- 2026-02-18: nf4 runs complete; cost per 1M tokens dropped ~28% at batch 8; perplexity delta +1.8% on long-form set.
- 2026-02-22: kv cache experiments (simulated hit 25/50/75) show near-linear savings until ~60% then taper.

If this reads OK I can: export the canonical spreadsheet to the shared sims folder, push a small parsing helper to the repo, and schedule a short sync with SRE to determine production telemetry needed for accurate cost-modeling.

End of draft.
